entries.source: American Physical Society, Physical Review D volume 75 issue 12
entries.notes: Published 29 June 2007. Hartle and Srednicki warn against a selection fallacy that treats observers as physically randomly sampled without an explicit basis for that assumption; cited to distinguish a credence rule from a literal sampler.

The arXiv manuscript was first posted in 2010 and the Journal of Physics: Conference Series version appears in volume 462 (2013), article 012050. Their xerographic distribution is a probability distribution for our location among otherwise compatible instances; the manuscript now treats its finite self-location kernel as the same kind of object rather than claiming a new construction.

entries.source: American Physical Society, Physical Review Research volume 2 issue 3
entries.notes: Published 22 September 2020. Garisto explicitly introduces a formalism to expose observer-selection assumptions and distinguishes selecting an observer by picking from versus being in a set of worlds. Cited as close peer-reviewed prior art for observer-selection formalization, not as support for this paper's mathematical theorems.
